GRIEVANCE XII ◆ LIBERTY AND DUE PROCESS

He has transformed the threshold of a court into an occasion for arrest, deterring people from seeking judgment.

THE RECORD SHOWS

Immigration agents arrested people appearing for required court proceedings, a practice later struck down by a federal district court.

Reporting described arrests at immigration hearings and firings of judges. On October 1, 2026, a federal court invalidated an ICE courthouse-arrest policy. The administration has defended expedited enforcement as necessary to carry out immigration law.

A DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE

3 MILESTONES
  1. 2025Immigration officers made arrests outside required immigration court hearings, raising concerns about discouraging attendance.
  2. February 2026A DHS policy expanded potential detention of previously admitted refugees before permanent-residence decisions.
  3. October 1, 2026A federal district court struck down a nationwide ICE policy concerning courthouse civil arrests.

WHAT THE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH

The February refugee directive is related context for changes to enforcement policy, not part of the October courthouse ruling. The district court’s decision may be appealed.
